title: Speech: The President's Address at the Entrance Ceremony
titleJp: 入社式[にゅうしゃしき]での式辞[しきじ]

sentences.jp: 新入[しんにゅう]社員[しゃいん]の皆[みな]さん、入社[にゅうしゃ]おめでとうございます。
sentences.en: To all of our new employees: congratulations on joining the company.

sentences.jp: 本日[ほんじつ]、こうして皆[みな]さんを新[あら]たな仲間[なかま]としてお迎[むか]えできることを、社員[しゃいん]一同[いちどう]を代表[だいひょう]して心[こころ]より嬉[うれ]しく思[おも]います。
sentences.en: On behalf of all our staff, I am truly delighted to be able to welcome you here today as our new colleagues.

sentences.jp: 今年[ことし]の新入[しんにゅう]社員[しゃいん]は八十二名[はちじゅうにめい]、そのうち十一名[じゅういちめい]は海外[かいがい]出身[しゅっしん]の方々[かたがた]です。
sentences.en: This year we have eighty-two new employees, eleven of whom come from overseas.

sentences.jp: 国籍[こくせき]も専攻[せんこう]も異[こと]なる皆[みな]さんが、それぞれの道[みち]を経[へ]てここに集[つど]ったこと自体[じたい]に、私[わたし]は当社[とうしゃ]の未来[みらい]を見[み]る思[おも]いがいたします。
sentences.en: In the very fact that you, with different nationalities and fields of study, have each followed your own path to gather here, I feel I can see our company's future.

sentences.jp: さて、晴[は]れの日[ひ]に水[みず]を差[さ]すようですが、皆[みな]さんにはまず、「すぐに役[やく]に立[た]とうとしなくてよい」ということをお伝[つた]えしたい。
sentences.en: Now, it may seem like throwing cold water on this happy day, but the first thing I want to tell you is this: you don't need to try to be useful right away.

sentences.jp: 意外[いがい]に思[おも]われるかもしれません。
私[わたし]自身[じしん]、三十年[さんじゅうねん]以上[いじょう]前[まえ]に入社[にゅうしゃ]した当初[とうしょ]は、一日[いちにち]も早[はや]く一人前[いちにんまえ]になろうと焦[あせ]るあまり、わからないことをわからないと言[い]えずに、かえって周囲[しゅうい]に迷惑[めいわく]をかけてばかりいました。
sentences.en: When I myself first joined the company more than thirty years ago, I was so anxious to become fully competent as quickly as possible that I couldn't admit when I didn't understand something, and ended up constantly causing trouble for the people around me.

sentences.jp: そんな私[わたし]に、当時[とうじ]の上司[じょうし]がかけてくれた言葉[ことば]があります。
sentences.en: There are some words my boss at the time said to me back then.

sentences.jp: 「新人[しんじん]の最大[さいだい]の武器[ぶき]は、知[し]らないことだ。知[し]らないからこそ、我々[われわれ]が当[あ]たり前[まえ]だと思[おも]い込[こ]んでいることに疑問[ぎもん]を持[も]てる」。
sentences.en: "A newcomer's greatest weapon is not knowing. Precisely because you don't know, you can question the things we take for granted."

sentences.jp: この言葉[ことば]は、今[いま]も私[わたし]の仕事[しごと]の根幹[こんかん]にあります。
sentences.en: Those words remain at the core of how I work to this day.

sentences.jp: 組織[そしき]というものは、長[なが]く続[つづ]けば続[つづ]くほど、慣習[かんしゅう]が理由[りゆう]を失[うしな]ったまま残[のこ]り続[つづ]けるものです。
sentences.en: The longer an organization exists, the more its customs tend to linger on even after the reasons for them have been lost.

sentences.jp: 「なぜこうするのですか」という皆[みな]さんの素朴[そぼく]な問[と]いこそが、そうした惰性[だせい]を揺[ゆ]さぶり、組織[そしき]に新[あたら]しい風[かぜ]を吹[ふ]き込[こ]む力[ちから]となるのです。
sentences.en: It is precisely your simple questions, "Why do we do it this way?", that have the power to shake up that inertia and breathe new life into the organization.

sentences.jp: どうか、遠慮[えんりょ]なく問[と]い、遠慮[えんりょ]なく失敗[しっぱい]してください。
sentences.en: So please, ask questions without hesitation, and fail without hesitation.

sentences.jp: その代[か]わり、失敗[しっぱい]したときには一人[ひとり]で抱[かか]え込[こ]まず、必[かなら]ず周[まわ]りに相談[そうだん]すること――これだけは約束[やくそく]していただきたい。
sentences.en: In return, when you do fail, don't keep it to yourself; always talk to the people around you. This one thing I would like you to promise me.

sentences.jp: 先輩[せんぱい]社員[しゃいん]は皆[みな]、かつては同[おな]じように右[みぎ]も左[ひだり]もわからない新人[しんじん]でした。
sentences.en: All of your senior colleagues were once newcomers who, just like you, didn't know left from right.

sentences.jp: 皆[みな]さんの問[と]いに、きっと真剣[しんけん]に向[む]き合[あ]ってくれるはずです。
sentences.en: I am sure they will take your questions seriously.

sentences.jp: 結[むす]びに、皆[みな]さんがこの会社[かいしゃ]で、仕事[しごと]を通[つう]じて自[みずか]らを大[おお]きく育[そだ]てていかれることを心[こころ]より願[ねが]い、私[わたし]の式辞[しきじ]といたします。
sentences.en: In closing, I sincerely hope that you will grow greatly through your work here at this company, and with that I conclude my address.

questions.q: What is the first thing the president wants to tell the new employees?
choices: They should work hard to be useful as quickly as possible
They don't need to try to be useful right away
They should never make mistakes in their first year
They should follow the company's customs closely

questions.q: According to the president's former boss, what is a newcomer's greatest weapon?
choices: Not knowing, which allows them to question assumptions

questions.q: What does the president ask the new employees to promise?
choices: To stay with the company for at least ten years
To ask permission before asking questions
To fix their mistakes on their own
To consult the people around them when they fail
